evidence.section_title: GOING BEYOND RELATIONSHIP STATUS:  A CROSS-SECTIONAL AND LONGITUDINAL  INVESTIGATION OF THE ROLE OF  SATISFACTION WITH RELATIONSHIP STATUS IN  PREDICTING POLISH YOUNG ADULTS' MENTAL  HEALTH
evidence.quote: [/page/0/Text/4] Cross-sectional findings from wave 1 carried out on a sample of 317 Polish young adults aged 20 to 35 (M = 23.46, SD = 3.04) revealed that higher satisfaction with relationship status predicted higher life satisfaction, higher emotional and psychological well-being, and lower depressive symptoms after controlling for gender, age, and education. Results of the longitudinal wave 2 ran on a subsample from wave 1 (N = 102) partially replicated the results obtained in wave 1 and demonstrated that satisfaction with relationship status at T1 was predictive of life satisfaction at T2, but it was not predictive of emotional and psychological well-being, and depressive symptoms at T2.
